name: 03-dose-change-buried
description: Lisinopril was doubled during admission but the discharge list shows the new dose with no CHANGED marker — the narrative mentions it once, mid-paragraph. Missing the change and re-verifying the old dose is exactly the wrong-medication-fact critical. The new dose must supersede, never overwrite.

PRINCIPAL DIAGNOSIS: Hypertensive urgency
SECONDARY: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, CKD stage 3, hyperlipidemia

HOSPITAL COURSE:
79 y/o Spanish-speaking female presented to ED with headache and BP 208/104. No focal neuro deficits; CT head negative. Admitted for BP management. Home antihypertensive regimen reviewed and adherence confirmed with daughter via interpreter — pharmacy fill records consistent. Given persistent stage 2 readings on home regimen, lisinopril was uptitrated to 20 mg daily on hospital day 2 with good response; BPs on day of discharge 138-148 systolic. contradictions.detail: Verified lisinopril fact says 10 mg daily; discharge documents uptitration to 20 mg daily (narrative, hospital day 2)

mustNot: extract lisinopril as 10 mg or as unchanged — the change is stated in the narrative even though the list has no CHANGED marker
overwrite the verified lisinopril fact — the 20 mg proposal supersedes it only after human verification
propose a change to metformin or any med that did not change
